pub async fn nested(start: f64) -> Result {
The signal and the button are there so the fixture measures a LIVE nesting
island rather than a static one: the claim is that nesting does not break
reactivity, and a fixture with nothing to click could not see that it had.
The nested components are deliberately NOT reactive -- a `Sig<T>` prop and
`$(...)` as a prop value are separate unlanded features (07/NOTES.md), and
folding them in would make one failure look like the other.

expected.$keys: The hydration keys in ALLOCATION order, RELATIVE to the render id: run.mjs prefixes `${mount.dataset.tk}.`. Read them as: the island's own template root spends root slot 0 -> `0`; the `labelled_card` call spends slot 1, so its context id is `1` and its <section> root takes `10`; the `badge` call inside spends slot 1 of THAT context, so its context is `11` and the <span> takes `110`. Byte for byte the sequence keys-nested.json records for case `07b-nested-in-element`, which run.mjs asserts on every run.
expected.$keysNotDocumentOrder: Allocation order, NOT document order. The two coincide here because nothing is passed as child content; they would NOT coincide for the `children_component` shape, where the child is built before the boundary and ends up carrying a lower key while sitting inside the element with the higher one (keys-nested.json `getterChildren`). lib/keys.mjs recovers allocation order from the key strings, so this list stays right either way.
expected.$components: Component boundaries in the source: `labelled_card` and the `badge` inside it. This is what makes the key check tight -- a well-formed key from the wrong depth parses fine on its own and is only wrong against a declared boundary count. See lib/keys.mjs.
expected.$templates: Template roots the compiled module declares: the island's own, plus one per component body. The counter fixture asserts exactly 1; this one must not, which is the single-island assumption run.mjs has to drop when this fixture goes live.
expected.$islandTemplate: MEASURED, not predicted, and it contradicts run.mjs's default of 0: the emitter declares the two COMPONENT body templates before the island's own, so the island root is the third of the three this island reaches (tmpl$h20207ec50a9647a8 the badge span, tmpl$h7cd76cfa254e7097 the card section, tmpl$h424d16885beec833 the island div). This is exactly the scaffold assumption run.mjs's template-order diagnostic exists to catch, and it was wrong.
expected.$hydrateMutations: Same target as the counter, and the same reason: a correctly claimed hole is a no-op. A component boundary adds no node of its own, so nesting must not change this number. If it is not 0 when this goes live, the nesting opened a context the server did not.
expected.$htmlAfterHydrate: null means the mount must serialize identically before and after hydration.
expected.$clickMutations: As the counter: upstream writes .data on the text node between the markers. The nested components hold no signal, so a click must not touch them at all.
expected.$clickHtml: The count element after one click. PREDICTED, not captured -- confirm on the first live run.
